summary: South Korean Interim Government Activities No. 27 covers December 1947 (some economic series end in November) and was prepared by the National Economic Board for USAMGIK. The month was dominated by an electric power emergency after North Korea capped deliveries to South Korea at 80,000 KW, leading to the Emergency Electric Power Board, coal and briquette shortages and curtailed railroad service. Rice collection reached 96.3 percent of quota, while refugees from the north fell to 4,487. Politically, the report covers the assassination of Dr. Chang Duk Soo, the transfer of terrorism cases to American military courts, the Helmick-KILA dispute, the founding of the National Independence Federation, Rhee and Kim Koo merger talks, and preparations for the UN Temporary Commission. Statistical tables on prices, trade, finance, banking, labor, health, education, and Korean National Youth membership give historians a detailed economic and administrative baseline for the last weeks before the 1948 elections.
highlights: North Korea notified on 25 November that South Korea must keep its draw within 80,000 KW; a seven-member Emergency Electric Power Board with legal force and a priority list (waterworks, coal mines, hospitals, railways) was created on 15 December.

Refugees from north of the 38th parallel numbered 4,487 in December, the lowest since February, bringing 1947 to 163,253 against 185,441 in 1946; about 60 percent of May-December arrivals went to Seoul or Kyonggi-do.

Rice collection reached 96.29 percent of the 5,156,000 suk quota (744,793 metric tons), but Cholla-pukto managed only 77.17 percent, and the Korean Interim Legislative Assembly heard complaints that quotas and the 640-won price were too harsh.

Bank of Chosun note issue reached 33,388 million won, nearly 13 billion more than at end of September, driven by rice-collection financing; the Seoul retail index stood roughly 19 times its August 1945 base.

Dr. Chang Duk Soo, political head of the Korean Democratic Party, was assassinated in early December; his killers were arrested 4 December, and Military Governor Dean transferred the Dai Han Min Chung terrorism case to a military court.

The moderate National Independence Federation, a 15-party body under Dr. Kimm Kiu Sic, was inaugurated on 20 December, while Rhee Syngman and Kim Koo's merger announcement stalled and parties split over the coming UN Commission and a South-only election.

The Legislative Assembly passed the Law Dealing with Public Theatrical Performances, rejected a no-confidence resolution 35 to 27, held a first reading of a land reform bill limiting holdings to 3 chungbo, and marked its first anniversary on 12 December.

The Agricultural Improvement Service was created on 15 December under Ordinance No. 160, and the National Venereal Disease Center opened in Seoul on 3 December; cholera fell to 14 cases in 1947 from 15,748 in 1946.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover of No. 27 (December 1947) prepared by the National Economic Board, map of Korea, and the six-part table of contents ending with Korean National Youth, Inc.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.summary: Figures are for December except Transportation, Communications, Industrial Production, Mining and Imports/Exports (November); the report is largely American-prepared, with Koreanization of statistics growing.

sections.title: Part I: Basic Aspects
sections.summary: Population movement, including 4,487 refugees from the north in December, and the Office of Property Custody's corporate reorganization, loan guarantees and Koreanization of vested property.

sections.title: Section 1. Population
sections.summary: Refugees from North Korea fell to 4,487 in December (163,253 for 1947); 21,916 Koreans were apprehended trying to enter Japan; Foreign Affairs handled Japanese, Chinese and travel matters.

sections.title: Refugees
sections.summary: December arrivals were the lowest since February 1947 but seven times December 1946; tables give monthly counts, origin by province and the four refugee camps.

sections.title: Distribution
sections.summary: Plan for processing and dispersing refugees; about 60 percent of May-December arrivals went to Seoul or Kyonggi-do, with yen over 1,000 deposited in blocked accounts.

sections.title: Japanese Affairs
sections.summary: Thirty-six Japanese remained in essential posts; two Korean-owned ships returned from Japan; SCAP extended Category II property claims to 30 June 1948.

sections.title: Chinese Affairs
sections.summary: Permits issued to 91 Chinese for travel to China (798 cumulative); 27 Chinese junks arrived at Inchon; four Korean students cleared for Nanking.

sections.title: U.S.-European Affairs
sections.summary: Travel orders for 19 students to the United States in December (111 in 1947) and four athletes bound for the St. Moritz Winter Olympics; weekly refugee chart follows.

sections.title: Section 2. Office of Property Custody (Vested Property)
sections.summary: Corporate reorganization of Seoul firms (285 under investigation), 235 million won in guaranteed loans, 16 property sales worth 5.2 million won, and royal estates passing to SKIG control from 1 January 1948.

sections.title: Part II: Production and Supply
sections.summary: Rice collection and food stocks, prices, agriculture, coal and minerals, industrial output, allocations, trade and labor, all shaped by power and coal shortages and by fertilizer and grain imports.

sections.title: Section 1. Food Supply
sections.summary: Rice collection reached 96.29 percent of quota; 586,419 tons of rice on hand at year end; 34,804 tons of grain imported; about 225,000 tons of imports projected for 1949.

sections.title: Rice Collection
sections.summary: Quota table by province (Cholla-pukto only 77.17 percent) and National Food Administration reports on poor-farmer rationing in Chungchong-namdo, a Seoul fraud case and Kyongsang-pukto delays.

sections.title: The Outlook
sections.summary: 1947 crop estimates and a Department of Agriculture memo projecting 350,000 tons of imports for 1948, with scheduled monthly arrivals of 10,000 to 34,000 tons and calorie targets.

sections.title: Section 2. Prices
sections.summary: Seoul retail index for 26 goods stood about 19 times the August 1945 level, driven by note issue and North Korean currency conversion; wholesale prices rose on power and coal shortages.

sections.title: Section 3. Agriculture, Forestry, and Fisheries
sections.summary: 1948 goals plan 3,211,844 chungbo cropped; Agricultural Improvement Service created 15 December (Ordinance 160); 220,953 tons of fertilizer shipped; fuelwood quotas set for Seoul.

sections.title: Agricultural Economics Bureau
sections.summary: Completed 1948 Production Goals with 3,211,844 chungbo available, 97 percent of the 1940-44 cropped area, and compared 1947 goals with harvests.

sections.title: Agricultural Production Bureau
sections.summary: Livestock goals, a breeding station planned on Cheju-do, 70 tons of pig bristles, apple exports, and cotton collection of about 2,020 tons.

sections.title: Forestry Bureau
sections.summary: Six provinces assigned 12,100 tons of charcoal and 1,764,000 cords of fuelwood for Seoul's winter; saltern permits to be coordinated with forestry.

sections.title: Fisheries Bureau
sections.summary: Canned marine products for June-November reported; deals concluded for 1,000 tons of anchovy and 100 tons of glue seaweed for Japan.

sections.title: Korean Agricultural Association
sections.summary: 220,953 tons of fertilizer shipped to railheads by 20 December and 196,095 received; 1948 allocation of 221,718 long tons secured after SCAP adjustment.

sections.title: Agricultural Research and Education
sections.summary: Ordinance 160 text: board of six voting members, transfer of experiment stations and the Suwon and Taegu agricultural colleges, and a National Extension Service.

sections.title: Four-H Clubs
sections.summary: Kyonggi-do 4-H activities: a dairy-farm school at Anyang for ten boys every two weeks, a straw-product contest and a rat campaign.

sections.title: Vested Property
sections.summary: Table 6 counts 325 vested companies under Department of Agriculture control in South Korea at 31 December 1947: 79 textile, 96 marine and 150 forest (128 provincial sawmills); field-office counts incomplete.

sections.title: Section 4. Mining and Minerals
sections.summary: November anthracite output fell 5.3 percent; 134.5 million won subsidy for Samchuk, Hwasun and Eunsung mines; only 64,823 tons of bituminous coal imported; copper mines under review.

sections.title: Coal
sections.summary: Anthracite and lignite output, stockpiles, Coal Committee allocations and bituminous imports from Japan, hampered by power shortage, truck-tire shortage and scarce briquettes.

sections.title: Metals
sections.summary: Pitch shortage, Taichong gold mine repossessed, copper mines owing about 37.2 million won net, Kobayashi tungsten sales of 241.45 million won, and production tables.

sections.title: Section 5. Industrial Production
sections.summary: Under 10 percent of 2,012 factories report; November flour fell 24.3 percent, cotton yarn 13.2 percent and paper 22.2 percent, and the cement plant sat idle most of the month.

sections.title: Processed Food
sections.summary: Flour milling in two vested mills fell 24.3 percent; Korean-owned mills milled 210 tons; noodle output recovered by 65 percent.

sections.title: Textiles
sections.summary: Cotton yarn fell 13.2 percent and cloth 15.7 percent from October as raw cotton ran short; reporting yarn mills rose from seven to nine.

sections.title: Paper
sections.summary: Machine-made paper fell 22.2 percent; Chosun Paper Mill at Sunchon dropped 78 percent amid material shortages.

sections.title: Hardware
sections.summary: Nail production in three vested plants was the second best of the year, only slightly under October.

sections.title: Chemical Group
sections.summary: Briquettes limited by pitch, coke at under one-third of the May-June rate, 1,722 tons of cement at Samchuk, plus brick, pottery and rubber items.

sections.title: Monopoly Bureau Products
sections.summary: No government salt output in November-December and private output fell in December; cigarette production down 15 percent while tobacco purchases exceeded budget.

sections.title: Section 6. Allocations and Distribution
sections.summary: Surplus Army clothing to be dyed at Chosun Boseki; FFA distributed 89.8 million won of goods; about 2,000,000 gallons of emergency kerosene ordered; kimchi salt ration cut to 2.7 kg.

sections.title: Allocations, Civilian Supplies
sections.summary: Clothing consigned to Internal Security, 15,881 kg of scrap metal, Australian wool, scrap rubber and equipment allocated to agencies.

sections.title: Allocations, Materials Control Corporation
sections.summary: Captured stockpiles reallocated, including 200 tons of Chinese copper coins and Kobayashi Mining bismuth, tungsten and graphite stocks.

sections.title: Allocations, Korean Produced Commodities
sections.summary: Tables of cloth, textiles, shoes, tires, soap, matches, cement and beer allocated through mid-December; allocations dropped sharply.

sections.title: Distribution, Korean Produced Commodities
sections.summary: FFA and FDA distributed 89,820,257 won in December and 1,208,526,920 won since July 1946; FFA purchases fell 60 percent while FDA purchases rose seven-fold.

sections.title: Petroleum
sections.summary: Order for about 2,000,000 gallons of emergency kerosene, gasoline allocations raised 25 percent, kerosene doubled, and over 20,000 empty drums stranded by the rail shortage.

sections.title: Salt
sections.summary: Kimchi salt ration cut from 3.9 to 2.7 kg per person in 1947; a 1.2 kg soya sauce ration advanced.

sections.title: Section 7. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Estimated December imports of 203 million won against exports of 276.7 million; Pusan took 48.2 percent of November imports; 988,344 tons arrived under Civilian Supply in 1947.

sections.title: Private Trade
sections.summary: November private imports of 463 million won, 80-90 percent via Hong Kong; exports mostly sea products, plus ship cargoes and Indian cotton purchases.

sections.title: Government to Government Transactions
sections.summary: Exports to Japan worth $134,389 in December, 100 tons of glue seaweed accepted by SCAP, and lead and zinc concentrates toll-smelted in Japan.

sections.title: Korean Items for Americans in Korea
sections.summary: Souvenirs sold to the Army Post Exchange reached $27,193.63 in December and $64,701.38 over five months.

sections.title: Imports, Civilian Supply
sections.summary: 988,344 tons received in 1947, Yosu port opened 15 November; December receipts included 102,787 tons of salt, 18,443 tons of ammonium nitrate and 61,863 tons of bituminous coal.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Labor Department reorganized into four bureaus; power-shortage orders suspended Child Labor and working-hours laws; Kyongsang Textile dispute; 193 reporting unions with 58,556 members.

sections.title: Part III: Public Services
sections.summary: Railroad cutbacks from coal shortage, communications finances, the electric power emergency and its board, public works, and low-cost and refugee housing.

sections.title: Section 1. Transportation
sections.summary: Bituminous coal shortage forced removal of 58 trains in November; transport receipts fell 21 percent; creosoted ties shipped from Agasaki; marine revenue rose 44 percent.

sections.title: Railroads
sections.summary: Rail income fell for the first time in five months; 49 passenger schedules cancelled, freight down 25,000 tons, fewer locomotive repairs, and briquette and power problems.

sections.title: Marine Transportation
sections.summary: Marine income rose 44 percent partly from late manifests; ships to carry a 45-day food supply from 1 January 1948.

sections.title: Highway and Air Transportation
sections.summary: Highway and air spending fell; 1,000 tires from Japan and automotive supplies expedited for the rice collection.

sections.title: Section 2. Communications
sections.summary: Receipts rose 18 percent in November on higher telephone rates; expenditures up 8 million won; exchanges inspected for emergency power; 41,000,000 Japanese stamps ordered destroyed.

sections.title: Revenue and Expenditures
sections.summary: Telephone income rose 7.3 million won, stamp sales dipped after higher rates, and spending rose on pole handling, supplies and interest.

sections.title: Employment
sections.summary: Staff rose by 17 persons in November, all in telephone and telegraph; tables of employees and government income handed to Finance.

sections.title: Postal Deposits and Insurance
sections.summary: Postal deposits fell while depositors rose slightly; book-transfer balances up 6 million won; insurance in force up 3 percent but policyholders declining.

sections.title: Telephone and Telegraph
sections.summary: Telephone revenue 171 percent above September under the 1 October rate schedule; telegraph revenue high despite fewer messages.

sections.title: Activities
sections.summary: Inspections of Seoul Central and Tong Dai Moon exchanges found faulty emergency generators; repeater technician course held 11-20 December; Pusan telegraph absenteeism noted.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Utilities
sections.summary: North Korea limited power to 80,000 KW; a seven-member Emergency Electric Power Board with legal force set priorities; plants ran at about 20 percent capacity; 130-134 streetcars operated.

sections.title: Section 4. Public Works
sections.summary: Man-days fell one-fourth and spending one-third; Andong and Namchang bridge projects inaugurated; 15 of 26 miles of Seoul-Suwon paving done; 248 fires caused 244.7 million won of losses.

sections.title: Section 5. Housing
sections.summary: A 40-house low-cost project in Seoul was completed and occupied; 200 winterized tents and a 400-house refugee project nearly finished; refugee housing progress tabulated by province.

sections.title: Part IV: Finance
sections.summary: Bank note issue, supplemental budgets and tax collection problems, bank deposits, rice-collection loans and insurance activity.

sections.title: Section 1. Government Finance
sections.summary: Note issue at 33,388 million won; SKIG deficit of 2,747 million since October; 629 million won of supplemental appropriations approved; revenue only 65 percent of approved budget.

sections.title: Note Issue of the Bank of Chosun
sections.summary: Circulation rose nearly 13 billion won since September because of rice collection; Civilian Supply accumulated 4,463 million won in deposits as a brake.

sections.title: Expenditure Budget and Revenue
sections.summary: Eight supplemental requests approved by the Military Governor; November revenue 1,225.1 million won, down 524.6 million from October; revenue 65 percent of budget.

sections.title: Taxation
sections.summary: Tax collection ran at 50-65 percent of projection; 30 employees finished an enforcement course on 27 December and provinces were radioed to speed collections.

sections.title: Civilian Supply Program
sections.summary: Table 6 shows Civilian Supply receipts of 298 million won (May-Dec 1946) rising to a 4.46 billion won balance by December 1947; 75 million won sat in fixed deposits, the rest at the Bank of Chosun.

sections.title: Section 2. Non-Government Finance
sections.summary: Deposits rose 2,569 million won in November; loans rose 16.2 billion won, mostly rice-collection credit; Finance directives on loan renewals and North Korean currency; life and damage insurance data.

sections.title: Cash Balances in Financial Institutions
sections.summary: Cash balances in financial institutions are driven mainly by seasonal demand rather than investment policy; text cut off at page end, so no figures given.

sections.title: Deposits in Financial Institutions
sections.summary: November deposits rose 2,569 million won, among the largest monthly rises since March 1946, including 1,302 million from the public.

sections.title: Loans by the Financial Institutions
sections.summary: Loan balances rose 16.2 billion won, including 7.2 billion government-guaranteed and over 7 billion in Bank of Chosun rediscounts for rice collection; insurance tables.

sections.title: Activities of Financial Institutions
sections.summary: Loans approved included 78,138 thousand won for agar-agar collection; directives covered loan renewal, North Korean cash, and a 3 billion won deposit campaign.

sections.title: Activities of Life Insurance Companies
sections.summary: Four Korean life insurers reinsured 307 policies for 12.4 million won in November; 63,320 holders of Japanese policies registered; new household fire policy requested.

sections.title: Part V: Government and Politics
sections.summary: Civil service and NEB actions, the Legislative Assembly, political realignment and the Chang assassination, legal affairs, police, and North-South interzone mail and Radio Pyongyang intercepts.

sections.title: Section 1. Administration
sections.summary: Helmick-KILA vetoes resolved; Civil Service ran courses and examinations (4,108 clerical candidates); NEB approved 432.9 million won extra for Police and a 120 million won bonus fund.

sections.title: Section 2. Korean Interim Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: Ten sessions averaged 66 members; theatrical law passed; no-confidence motion rejected 35 to 27; governors approved; land reform bill read; first anniversary on 12 December.

sections.title: Law Dealing with Public Theatrical Performances
sections.summary: Second reading approved Sections I-XVIII giving the Education Director power over permits, restrictions and fines up to 50,000 won, replacing Government-General Order 197.

sections.title: Legislative-Executive Misunderstanding
sections.summary: Helmick explained to the 180th session his non-concurrence in the Temporary Constitution and Anti-Collaborators Bill; the Assembly closed the issue by 41 to 9.

sections.title: Approval of Governors
sections.summary: Rules amended 44 to 0 so a majority of a quorum approves appointments; governors of Kangwon-do and Chungchong-namdo then approved by secret ballot.

sections.title: Rice Collection
sections.summary: Members Chong and Lee reported complaints of high quotas and the low 640-won purchase price; the Assembly took no action.

sections.title: Land Reform Bill
sections.summary: First reading of a bill dividing holdings above 3 chungbo, with compensation, 15-year installments and price at three times average annual yield.

sections.title: Other Business
sections.summary: Meatless Friday proposal, braille voting petition, failed no-confidence vote on the Outline of Measures, Public Act No. 8 delay, and anniversary speeches by Hodge and Helmick.

sections.title: Section 3. Political Developments
sections.summary: National Independence Federation inaugurated 20 December with 15 parties; Rhee and Kim Koo merger stalled; parties split on a South-only election; Rhee attacked General Hodge.

sections.title: National Independence Federation
sections.summary: Founded 20 December under Dr. Kimm Kiu Sic with five principles and six policies, including a North-South meeting and withdrawal of US and Soviet troops.

sections.title: Extreme Rightist Merger
sections.summary: Rhee and Kim Koo announced unity on 1-5 December, but the joint meeting was postponed; the merger principle was restated on 27 December.

sections.title: United Nations Commission
sections.summary: Rightists backed the UN Commission and a South election, leftists opposed it, and a reception committee under Police Director Chough was organized on 12 December.

sections.title: Council of Twelve Parties
sections.summary: A 6 December preparatory meeting for the ninth session was never followed up; the Korean Independence Party expelled three executives and deferred joining.

sections.title: Statements by Rhee, Syngman
sections.summary: Rhee criticized General Hodge on 5 and 16 December and demanded an immediate election, then approved Hodge's 17 December anti-Communist warning and quieted down.

sections.title: Section 4. Legal Affairs
sections.summary: Ordinances 158-160 published; opinions on Labor Mediation Board powers; prison population 20,718; Dai Han Min Chung terrorism case moved to military court; Chang Duk Soo trial recommended for a commission.

sections.title: Section 5. Police
sections.summary: Centralized police structure outlined; Chang Duk Soo's killers arrested 4 December; Chough ordered political neutrality; 170 arrested in Kyongsang-pukto over rice collection.

sections.title: Section 6. Interzone Activities
sections.summary: Mail exchanged at Tosang on 13 and 27 December; Radio Pyongyang praised North Korea's currency conversion and rejected the UN decision; Radio Moscow attacked US policy and MacArthur.

sections.title: Part VI: Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare, the education budget, culture, public information, a press digest, and Korean National Youth growing to 404,585 members.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: National Venereal Disease Center opened 3 December; cholera down to 14 cases in 1947; nutrition survey of 4,676 families; 57 refugee-camp tents winterized; Christmas aid for 4,000 children.

sections.title: Preventive Medicine
sections.summary: School tuberculin and X-ray survey began, venereal disease center opened, plague control and a rat school for 40, and typhus fell to 4 cases from 117.

sections.title: Veterinary Affairs
sections.summary: Swine plague killed 6,123 pigs in six provinces (about 123 million won loss); 58 horses given to police; Kyonggi dairy cattle tested free of tuberculosis.

sections.title: Pharmaceutical Affairs
sections.summary: 2,856 narcotic licenses issued, 13 raids in Seoul with 15 arrests, five X-ray generators allocated and 30 carloads of supplies shipped.

sections.title: Laboratories
sections.summary: Biologicals production tables for the Seoul and Anyang/Pusan veterinary institutes; 3,937,000 smallpox vaccinations produced; nutrition survey found farm families above 2,400 calories.

sections.title: Public Assistance
sections.summary: Examined 320 blind and deaf pupils and 2,000 children in 17 Seoul institutions; nine border refugee camps reviewed; Welfare Housing Plan one-third complete.

sections.title: Korean Red Cross
sections.summary: Ten chapters, five clinics and a 230-bed Seoul hospital; December disaster-relief and volunteer garment conferences; trucks lacking.

sections.title: Section 2. Education
sections.summary: 1948-49 education budget of 3,128,979,081 won, about 80 percent for common schools; advisors' conference 16-17 December; teacher certification from 1 January 1948; English institute with 594 students.

sections.title: Budget Estimate 1948-49
sections.summary: Requested budget of 3,128,979,081 won against 1,660,242,480 in 1947-48, aimed at universal schooling for the first three grades.

sections.title: Bureau of Handicapped Children
sections.summary: Blind and deaf schools enrolled 268 boys and 102 girls; equipment lacking; transfer to Education and a vocational committee for the blind.

sections.title: Teacher Certification
sections.summary: New rules effective 1 January 1948 grant permanent certificates only after specified professional training, called a major achievement of the year.

sections.title: American Language Institute
sections.summary: 252 day and 342 evening students; Seoul private English schools to meet minimum standards; three teaching syllabuses distributed.

sections.title: Bureau of Research
sections.summary: Lectures to the National Police College, probe of Rapid Realization Party adult schools, a school reporting plan, and test construction.

sections.title: Section 3. Culture
sections.summary: Historical survey of Korean literature; National Library used 291,285 times in 1947; Korea Symphony Orchestra to stage La Traviata; KBS broadcast 337 hours; skaters left for St. Moritz.

sections.title: Korean Literature
sections.summary: Survey from King Se-jo's 1487 Tong-moon-syen and the 1446 alphabet to Japanese suppression and current publishing despite paper shortage.

sections.title: National Library
sections.summary: About 800 readers daily; 291,285 books used and 265,275 readers in 1947; library school of 30 students and rare Yi Kyu Bo volumes.

sections.title: Art and Music
sections.summary: Symphony farewell concert for Ely Haimowitz on 2 December, Christmas programs, an ancient dance performance and a Kim Eun Ho exhibit.

sections.title: Korean Broadcasting System
sections.summary: 337 broadcast hours including Christmas programs, translated world dramas, and a 1,000-selection American transcription library.

sections.title: Miscellaneous
sections.summary: Three skaters left 7 December for St. Moritz; Royal Asiatic Society reorganized 18 December; W. P. Kim returned from the IPR London conference.

sections.title: Section 4. Public Information
sections.summary: Public Information issued 74 press releases including Dean's terrorism-case statement; Farmers' Weekly issues 86-88; a Nonsan Mobile Education train found only 35.8 percent saw Americans as beneficial.

sections.title: Bureau of Public Information
sections.summary: Special releases on terrorism cases, the UN Commission, power conservation and rice collection; Farmers' Weekly issues No. 86, 87 and 88 published.

sections.title: Bureau of Public Opinion
sections.summary: Registered 4 parties and 9 publications, suspended 3 publications, ran six opinion surveys and 11 lectures.

sections.title: Office of Civil Information
sections.summary: Mobile Education train visited Nonsan 6-8 December distributing 4,000 Farmers' Weekly; 99 photo panels and 133 cartons of books sent out.

sections.title: Section 5. Press and Public Opinion
sections.summary: Korean press digest on the Helmick-KILA dispute, Dean's military-court decision, Rhee's attacks, the National Independence Federation, the Chang murder, editor arrests and a women's alliance poll.

sections.title: The Deputy Military Governor and KILA
sections.summary: Papers printed KILA's questions on Helmick's vetoes and his reply; rightist papers split on dissolving KILA.

sections.title: The Military Governor and the Courts
sections.summary: Full text of Dean's 1 December statement transferring the Dai Han Min Chung case to a Military Court, with press reactions.

sections.title: Maneuvers of Political Parties
sections.summary: Rhee-Kim Koo accord reported then collapsed; the 12-14 December joint meeting was cancelled after the Chang assassination.

sections.title: National Independence Federation
sections.summary: Press coverage of the new moderate coalition, Rhee's sneer, and the 20 December meeting.

sections.title: Murder of Chang, Duk Soo
sections.summary: Assassination of the Democratic Party strategist overshadowed other news; Hodge promised military trials for such cases on 27 December.

sections.title: Police and the Press
sections.summary: Police roundups, 117 communications workers arrested, 46 officials charged with graft, and arrests of editors of Hyun Dai Ilbo and Dai Han Ilbo.

sections.title: Economic Matters
sections.summary: Papers blamed Military Government for inflation, protested imports, and debated the power shortage and North Korean currency change.

sections.title: Other Topics
sections.summary: Coverage of the Chinese UN Commission member's arrival, the failed London ministers' conference, and local matters such as rat-caused fires.

sections.title: Public Opinion Poll
sections.summary: Women's Alliance poll: 106 favored and 80 opposed a North-South leaders' meeting; 125 wanted the new Military Governor to check inflation.

sections.title: Section 6. Korean National Youth, Inc.
sections.summary: Membership reached 404,585 in December; Lee Bum Suk and Lee Chawn Chun of Dai Dong issued a joint truce statement on 11 December; 11,843,113 seedlings requisitioned for planting.
